summary: Stores run down old bag stock before a stricter bag law, then offer paid reusables.
realLife: A state closed the loophole that let thicker plastic bags count as reusable. A store ran out of its remaining plastic bags around New Year's Eve and was compliant the next day. A grocers' group said stores sold off bulk stock and moved to paper or canvas, and smaller stores faced higher bag costs, over a dollar each for paper, against margins near two percent. Advocates cited a study showing bag bans cut bags in the environment by a quarter to nearly half.
sources: Santa Barbara Independent (Santa Barbara, California), 'With Plastic Reusable Bags Gone, Santa Barbara Shoppers and Stores Adjust to California's New Bag Rules', January 10, 2026: https://www.independent.com/2026/01/10/with-plastic-reusable-bags-gone-santa-barbara-shoppers-and-stores-adjust-to-californias-new-bag-rules/
